problem: Existing ObjectNav, REVERIE and SOON benchmarks give the target explicitly (category label, referring expression or object reference). DDN covers implicit demands but lacks a paired diagnostic over phrasing and cue type, and ULN varies explicitness only for route following. So no benchmark measures whether agents can recover the goal from an indirect human need and carry it through active search.
motivation: People express needs indirectly ('the room feels stuffy'), so agents must infer the target object, find a unique scene instance and decide when to stop. A single success rate cannot show whether failure comes from phrasing, cue type, or a particular stage of the navigation chain. The paper therefore builds a benchmark with orthogonal language axes and stage-wise metrics.
key_idea: A diagnostic benchmark for intent-driven object navigation that hides the target name, pairs each of 500 intents with four instruction styles and four intent modes under matched geometry, and uses stage-wise metrics (IM, OSR, SR, GSR) to localize failures.
insight: The gap between neighborhood reach and terminal success dominates: OSR is 0.687 but SR is 0.249 and GSR is 0.055, so failures concentrate after arrival, in verification and localization. The explicit-target ablation raises SR only from 0.280 to 0.448 and GSR to 0.124, so inference is a real bottleneck but not the main one. Intent mode (event 0.287 vs affordance 0.185) matters more than phrasing style (spread of only 2.8 points), though per-intent consistency across styles is very low (CSR 5.6-9.6%).
method: Task formulation: episode e=(scene, free-text intent, fixed start pose, hidden target instance and category). The intent must not contain the target name and the target must be the unique admissible instance. Success is stopping within a radius of the target position.

Diagnostic axes: four instruction styles (formal, natural, casual, emotional) crossed with four intent modes (event-script, inner-state, physical-state, affordance). Mode labels reach 91.0% agreement and Cohen's kappa 0.86 on 100 double-annotated items.

Construction: automatic candidate generation over 176 VLNVerse Isaac Sim scenes gives 17,624 intent sets. Stratified selection, leakage control, VLM-judge scoring (Gemini) and human audit reduce this to 500 intents (2000 instructions, 64 categories).

Reference Agent: a fixed modular agent with a VLM for target-visibility and exploration direction, Grounding-DINO detection, evidence memory, waypoint planning on a navigable map, and termination on visual plus geometric evidence or a 30-step budget. Only the VLM backend is swapped.
Metrics: IM (synonym-matched category), SR@2m, OSR@2m, SPL, TL, GSR@1m (SR with final-frame target visibility), CSR (all four styles succeed), and gaps g_infer, g_term, g_prec, Δstyle, Δintent.
Explicit-target diagnostic: replaces the intent with the ground-truth category on the Gemini formal setting, holding everything else fixed.

setting.backbone: GPT-5.4, Qwen3.6-Plus, Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite (frozen, zero-shot VLMs) inside a fixed reference agent with Grounding-DINO
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D plus pose, with free-text intent
setting.action_space: waypoints on a navigable map plus a stop action, 30-step budget
setting.privileged: none at test time (the target category is hidden from the agent)

numbers.extra: 500 intents x 4 styles = 2000 episodes; SR/OSR/SPL at 2m, GSR at 1m; 30-step budget
numbers.evidence: Table 1 main full-benchmark results, GPT-5.4 row (IM 0.504, SR 0.249, GSR 0.051, OSR 0.691, SPL 0.078, TL 24.3)

numbers.eval_set_note: Gemini formal-style setting only (500 episodes); implicit intent replaced by ground-truth target category
numbers.extra: GT target category given (privileged); implicit formal condition for comparison: SR 0.280, GSR 0.066, OSR 0.706

numbers_note: Benchmark is new, so all rows are the paper's own reference-agent results; the split is not named officially (the fixed 500-intent split is used as 'test'). Style and mode breakdowns (Tables 2-3) are omitted from the numbers list.
results: Across three VLMs, IM is 0.483 and OSR 0.687, but SR@2m falls to 0.249 and GSR@1m to 0.055. Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite is best on SR (0.257), but the three models differ by only 1.6 SR points. Naming the target lifts SR only from 0.280 to 0.448, so terminal localization stays a major failure point.
limitations: Controlled simulation only: English single-target instructions, static apartments, no clarification dialogue, 30-step horizon, and a single reference agent.
IM relies on a finite synonym vocabulary, and the intents are rewritten and judged by automated VLMs, which limits diagnostic precision.
Only three VLMs are evaluated, with small inter-model differences; the released artifact excludes the full data assets and scene packages.
